author: Zhihui Yang

steps.title: Create or Sign Into NCBI Account
steps.instruction: Access the NCBI submission system to establish your user identity.

substeps.instruction: New users: Create an account using a 3rd party sign-in option.
Existing users: Sign in to your NCBI account via the 3rd party sign-in page (use 'more login options' if necessary).

steps.title: Establish a Data Level BioProject
steps.instruction: Create a new data level BioProject under the ViroTrakr umbrella BioProject to link your data submission.

substeps.instruction: Log into the BioProject Submission Portal.
Populate the 'Submitter' tab (using a laboratory submission group is highly recommended).
Populate the 'Project type' tab (e.g., select 'Raw sequence reads').
Populate the 'Target' tab using descriptive and valid organism names (e.g., 'Norwalk virus' instead of 'norovirus').
Populate the 'General Info' tab: select release date, provide a public description of study goals, and choose relevance.

In 'General Info', select 'Yes' for 'Is your project part of a larger initiative' and enter the appropriate ViroTrakr umbrella accession number: PRJNA433975 (norovirus), PRJNA433976 (hepatitis A), PRJNA433977 (sapovirus), PRJNA817226 (rotavirus), PRJNA817227 (astrovirus), or PRJNA817228 (hepatitis E).
Leave the 'BioSample' tab blank.
Leave the 'Publications' tab blank or add relevant publications.
Review and click 'Submit' in the 'Review and Submit' tab.

steps.title: Submit Raw Sequencing Data to SRA
steps.instruction: Submit raw sequencing data and create associated BioSamples via the SRA Submission Portal.

substeps.instruction: Log into the SRA Submission Portal and click 'New Submission'.
Populate the 'Submitter' tab.
Populate the 'General info' tab: enter the BioProject accession number from the previous step, select 'No' for existing BioSample, and choose a release date.

To enable automated human-read scrubbing: choose 'Release on specified date' (e.g., one week in the future) and email sra@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov requesting the human read scrubbing analysis flag for your BioProject (PRJNAXXXXXX).
Populate the 'BioSample Type' tab by selecting the appropriate package (e.g., 'One Health Enteric').
Populate the 'BioSample attributes' tab by downloading the Excel template, filling it out, and uploading it as a tab-delimited file.
Populate the 'SRA metadata' tab by downloading the Excel spreadsheet, filling out the 'SRA_data' tab with fastq filenames, and uploading it as a TSV file.
Upload sequence data via the 'Files' tab using FTP (e.g., FileZilla): connect using provided Host/Username/Password, create a required named subfolder, and upload files.
Return to the SRA submission page, click 'Select preload folder' (wait at least 10 minutes after upload), and click 'Continue'.
Review and submit to receive SRA accession numbers (SRRxxxxxxxx).

steps.title: Submit Assembled Data to GenBank
steps.instruction: Submit assembled sequences or consensus sequences to GenBank to ensure global availability and FAIR data-sharing.

substeps.instruction: Log into the GenBank Submission Portal and click 'New Submission'.
For Norovirus: Use the GenBank Submission Portal annotation pipelines.
For other foodborne viruses: Use alternate tools such as BankIt or tbl2asn.
Populate the 'Submission type' and 'Submitter' tabs.
Populate the 'Sequencing technology' tab: select 'Assembled sequences' and provide assembly program and version/date.
Populate the 'Sequences' tab: upload nucleotide FASTA files (.txt) and specify the release date.
Populate the 'Source Info' tab.

Populate the 'Source modifiers' tab to link to ViroTrakr: upload a tab-delimited table containing the BioSample and BioProject numbers (using the provided customized template or by emailing gb-admin@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov).
Review the submission in the 'Review & Submit' tab and click 'Submit' to receive GenBank accession numbers.
